transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I just feel like I got a motor running inside me all day. It's... I don't know, if I have to sit still, like at church, or out there in the clinic, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped. I just have to get up or do something. I can't just stay put.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or euphoric?

No, not really. I don't think I've ever felt unusually high or anything like that. I mean, my mood is mostly just normal. I just get really antsy and can't sit still, but I'm not walking around feeling super happy or euphoric, no.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?

Yeah, I do. Like... when folks are talking through ride times, or making pantry lists, or going over church plans, I listen good at first. But then my mind just slips off somewhere else. I end up missing pieces I really needed to hear, even when I'm trying my best to pay attention.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind over and over, even when you try to ignore them?
No, I can't say I do. I mean, my mind jumps around a lot, like I said, but it's not like the same thought gets stuck in my head over and over. I don't really have anything like that bothering me.
Did you have these same problems with sitting still or paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. It's pretty much always been this way. Back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always moving my seat around because I just could not stay put. I'd talk out of turn, and... well, I was always getting in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things?
No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about stuff like that. My mind is too busy jumping from one thing to the next to get stuck worrying about everyday chores or whatever.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of hyperactivity/restlessness and impaired sustained attention across multiple settings. He reports inability to remain seated, feeling driven to move, distractibility during conversations and planning tasks, and childhood school difficulties including leaving his seat and talking out of turn. The interview also reduces key alternatives: no euphoric mood suggestive of mania, no repetitive intrusive thoughts suggestive of OCD, and no generalized excessive worry. This is most consistent with disturbance of activity and attention (ADHD, predominantly hyperactive/inattentive features under ICD-10 F90.0).
